item.title: In 2024, MacKenzie Scott gave $2m each to 279 nonprofits in $640M giveaway after 6,000 applications
item.description: MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic initiative in 2024 selected 361 nonprofit organizations to receive $640 million. Through an open application process, more than 6,000 groups submitted requests for funding. The selected organizations focused on issues related to economic disparities, education, healthcare, and discrimination. Scott's approach shifted from private research to an open call, increasing both funding and recipients. This effort follows her significant charitable donations made after her divorce from Jeff Bezos.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1913, Ohio parents mailed their 10-pound baby to grandmother for 15 cents
item.description: In a remarkable incident from 1913, an Ohio couple made headlines by sending their eight-month-old son to his grandmother using Parcel Post, a groundbreaking and controversial method. The minimal cost of just 15 cents shocked the public and sparked a series of similar reports across the nation. Safety concerns led the Post Office Department to swiftly ban the practice, highlighting the intricate nature of rural life during that era.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NY woman’s 20-year apartment fight continues after court rejects landlord’s commercial lease claim
item.description: A landlord's attempts to reclaim a Manhattan apartment are hindered due to ongoing claims about rent stabilization. E. Terese Carpenter has resided in the unit for over 20 years, despite the existence of a commercial lease. The appeals court identified unresolved issues regarding the actual use of the apartment and the landlord's awareness of the situation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bangladesh wage protests: Clashes erupt between garment workers and police, dozens of factories shut
item.description: Tensions soared in Ashulia as garment workers rallied for higher wages, leading to confrontations with law enforcement. To maintain control, the police deployed tear gas to break up the protest after production was halted. Reports revealed that more than 50 factories chose to close temporarily amid the unrest, with indefinite shutdowns and sit-ins occurring in various industrial areas. This turmoil highlights the ongoing struggle for improved pay and working conditions.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Pennsylvania county sold home for $109,000 after notices went to dead owner; court sets sale aside
item.description: A Pennsylvania appeals court recently ruled to cancel a tax sale of a home in Garnet Valley. The tax sale occurred due to the county's failure to notify the correct property owner about unpaid taxes. Bonnie Wilson's home was sold despite her and her son Kevin both being deceased. The appeals court emphasized the need for tax bureaus to investigate further when notices are returned.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 7 killed as tribal feud over forest ownership triggers gunfight in Pakistan
item.description: Seven people were killed in a gunfight between the Gilal and Kaloch tribes over a decades-old forest ownership dispute in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, PTI reported, quoting police. The clash took place in Battagram district on Thursday night, leaving four members of the Gilal tribe and three from the Kaloch tribe dead. Repeated efforts to resolve the dispute have failed.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: Bangladesh violence: Fresh arson attacks reported as unrest continues amid Sheikh Hasina's return plans
item.description: Tensions continue to rise in Bangladesh as fresh arson attacks erupt in response to Sheikh Hasina's anticipated return. In an effort to restore peace following violent incidents that claimed multiple lives, paramilitary forces have been mobilized. Communication services in her hometown have resumed after disruptions caused by the unrest, while over a hundred Awami League members have been arrested in Dhaka.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: More than 100,000 strangers have shared handwritten stories anonymously
item.description: More than 100,000 anonymous handwritten stories have been shared in The Strangers Project since its inception. Individuals recount personal experiences centered on themes such as love, loss, and hope. Brandon Doman founded the project in 2009 to create a space for these shared experiences. The Strangers Project is currently located at the World Trade Center Oculus in New York City.
item.dc:creator: Smridhi Dang

item.title: NJ appeals $11.25M verdict for woman handcuffed during stroke by trooper
item.description: In a tragic turn of events, Cheryl Lynn Rhines suffered a severe stroke while driving and was mistakenly arrested for intoxication. The responding trooper overlooked the critical nature of her medical emergency, causing significant delays in her treatment. This negligence resulted in lasting brain injuries and communication issues for Rhines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Balochistan shutdown: Markets shut across Quetta as alliance protests rising inflation, insecurity
item.description: A significant shutdown swept across Quetta and several districts in Balochistan on Thursday, driven by widespread protests led by the All Parties Alliance. The strike aimed to highlight urgent issues such as deteriorating law and order, soaring unemployment rates, and rampant inflation. Major commercial hubs faced complete shutdowns, resulting in major disruptions.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Florida battles historic flooding as storms move further north
item.description: In Central Florida, residents face rising water levels from recent heavy rain, prompting evacuation alerts. Authorities urge those living by the St. Johns River to brace for potential evacuations as flooding disrupts Thanksgiving festivities. Emergency responders are tirelessly aiding those stranded in waterlogged neighborhoods, while meteorologists predict that both heavy rainfall and flooding risks will persist for the foreseeable future.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Pregnant at 34 weeks, New York nurse completes all seven major marathons
item.description: Deirdre Keane, an inspiring nurse practitioner from New York, achieved a remarkable feat in 2026 by completing all seven World Marathon Majors while pregnant. Approaching her training thoughtfully after learning about her pregnancy, she ran the New York City Marathon at 34 weeks, pushing boundaries she once thought were fixed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mexican cartel leaders, 19 others indicted in US over drug and arms trafficking
item.description: In a significant legal move, a federal grand jury has charged leaders of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel along with 19 associates. Key allegations against them include drug trafficking and weapons smuggling. Prominent figures Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga are on the run, purportedly using violence and bribery to grow their criminal empire and engage in human smuggling.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: After his wife Susan died, Warren Lewis learned her body cannot be donated to science because of this
item.description: Susan Lewis's noble desire to donate her body to science was thwarted by a miscommunication. After her passing, her husband, Warren Lewis, tirelessly advocated for revisions to the university's body donation policy. This advocacy birthed a collaboration with Macquarie University, enabling weekend donations and ensuring that future donors' wishes are honored, despite bureaucratic hurdles. Susan's journey underscores the complexities surrounding body donations in Australia.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Federal Lawsuit: Maine family challenges rooster fines; alleges free-speech violations
item.description: David and Sara LeBlanc have taken legal action against Ogunquit, Maine, after being penalized for setting up rooster sculptures outside their home. These sculptures symbolize support for their daughter Pyper, who is autistic and adores roosters. The town has classified the sculptures as commercial advertising for their restaurant, Omelette Factory, and although the couple has removed them, local residents have rallied to display the sculptures in unity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Air Niugini plane makes emergency landing in Philippines, all 146 safe
item.description: An incident occurred involving an Air Niugini aircraft with 146 individuals on board that indicated possible engine fire. The flight performed an emergency landing at Davao International Airport shortly after midnight. Passengers and crew were safely evacuated via emergency slides, with no injuries reported. Other flights at the airport were briefly suspended for safety checks and to assist those on the aircraft.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma
